title: Isolation - Mind Field (Ep 1)
beats: Imagine being locked in a bare 10x10 room for three days; psychologists warn of brain damage
Brain as hungry sponge; boredom as a weak form of disgust (Plutchik wheel); it drives neurogenesis
Study: people prefer pain to 15 minutes of boredom
Fake focus group: Jamison shocked, says never again, then alone with the button
He presses after 1:57; conclusion: any stimulation beats none
Social animals befriend a volleyball or a shock button
Sensory deprivation history: 1930s experiments, Cold War, float tanks
Michael floats an hour with Dominic Monaghan as a trial run; half-dreams with eyes open
Space travel motive; Stefania Follini's 130 days underground, lost body clock, underestimated time by half
Solitary confinement: William Brown tours a cell, 16 years in prison, five months in the hole
Setup: white room, constant light, Soylent, no clock; baseline vitals and cognitive tests
Doctors predict circadian disruption, jet-lag effects; Michael admits he is neurotic and scared
Day-by-day: he guesses the time repeatedly and drifts more wrong; counting, alphabet, steps as self-stimulation
Psychologists comment live: hunger and sleep unreliable clocks, a companion generated in the mind
Cinema of memories helps, then mood drops, confusion, incoherent thoughts, lost water bottles, a dream mistaken for reality
Observers worry: looks depressed, quiet, confused
Out at 72 h; blood pressure up; cognitive tests better than expected thanks to adrenaline, verbal test worst
Reunion with family: experience is fully had only when shared; reframes proverb about travelling furthest with others

metrics.misconception: partial: assumption that being alone with yourself is easy; 'preferring shock' demonstration, and the narrator's own claim that distractions were easy to lose but people were not
metrics.brute_force: yes 14:03: lives the experiment literally for 72 h
metrics.examples: 4 case studies, rising from a 30-min button test to an hour float to others' 130 days and years to his own 72 h
metrics.ending: Moral insight: experience is completed by sharing; proverb reinterpreted

principles.1: confirmed: boredom, a room, a phone; everyone knows boredom
principles.2: confirmed: only Plutchik wheel introduced, briefly (1:30)
principles.4: partly: 'hungry sponge' brain analogy at 0:55; mostly experience not analogy
principles.5: confirmed: the video is the problem acted out literally, by a stranger (2:23) and by Michael (14:03-29:51)
principles.6: confirmed: the 'brute force' is the literal experiment before any explanation; measured by baseline tests
principles.7: confirmed: viewer sees time guesses fail repeatedly (18:36, 20:04, 22:23, 23:15) and infers loss of circadian cue
principles.8: partly: speech steady; slowdown by expanding story beats and long silent diary stretches rather than words per minute
principles.9: confirmed: repeated time-guess check-ins and counting rituals across days
principles.10: confirmed: 2-minute button test, 1 hour float, 130-day cave, 72-hour room
principles.11: partly: boredom definition, fake study, float tank are stepping stones to the room; ordering is deliberate
principles.12: confirmed: Plutchik, Harvard/Virginia study, NASA Follini, Cold War, solitary confinement
principles.13: partly: plain language with expert voices, no explicit tool-choice reasoning

new_moves.what: An unsuspecting subject plays out the hypothesis on camera before it is named

new_moves.name: stepping-stone-ordeal
new_moves.what: Shorter trial (float) before the full experiment to raise stakes and give the viewer calibrated expectation

new_moves.name: live-expert-commentary-on-subject

new_moves.what: Presenter is the lab rat with baseline and post-test measures

theory: Mind Field teaches by running the experiment, not describing it: a fake study predicts the result, a trial run calibrates, then the presenter lives the full version while experts annotate. Insight is discovered via repeated check-ins and measurable drift, and the lesson lands emotionally with a reframed proverb.
velocity: Scene builder: experiment-replay scene with repeated check-ins that visibly accumulate error (the clock-guess drift)
Orchestrator: run a quick predict-then-reveal trial before the explanation
Ghost hands: show the learner acting as the subject, timing guesses against truth
Evals: compare learner's prediction before and after the reveal
Voice: expert-commentary track as a second voice annotating live data
quote: he who travels furthest travels with others
